title: Kenya Airways Acting CEO George Kamal Resigns
desc: Kenya Airways Acting CEO George Kamal has resigned, with Habil Waswani set to take over in an acting capacity from September 15.
content:
Kenya Airways is facing another leadership transition after Acting Group Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer Capt. George Kamal resigned from the national carrier for personal reasons.

The airline announced the development on Tuesday, saying Kamal will remain in office during a 30-day transition period before formally leaving Kenya Airways on September 30, 2026.

Kamal has served as Acting Group Managing Director and CEO since December 16, 2025, after previously working as the airline's Chief Operating Officer.

During his time in executive leadership, Kenya Airways credited him with helping stabilise operations and supporting the implementation of its turnaround strategy.

The Board has appointed Habil Waswani, the airline's Company Secretary and Director of Legal Services and Regulatory Compliance, as the next Acting Group Managing Director and CEO.

Waswani is expected to assume the acting role on September 15 as the airline begins another phase of its leadership transition.

Kenya Airways has also started the process of recruiting a substantive Group Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer.

The leadership change comes at an important time for the national carrier as it continues efforts to strengthen its operations and manage financial and operational challenges.

For travellers and the wider business community, leadership stability at Kenya Airways remains important because the airline plays a major role in connecting Kenya with regional and international markets.

A change at the top does not immediately mean changes to scheduled flights or passenger services. However, the incoming leadership will play an important role in guiding the airline's operations and longer-term strategy.

Waswani brings experience from his work in legal, regulatory and corporate matters at Kenya Airways, where he has served for more than five years.

Attention will now turn to the transition process and the Board's search for a permanent CEO.

For Kenya Airways, the immediate task will be ensuring continuity during the handover while maintaining progress on its turnaround plans and day-to-day operations.

The Board's eventual choice of a substantive CEO will also be closely watched as the national carrier seeks to navigate its next chapter.
